hunk.before:
C-before and the MCP verification connection. It runs the unchanged
`freshFixtureProofSql` using B's actual PID, XID and observations. That proof must
observe B aborted, both observed-key scopes absent, and the real marker absent.
The four original sealed writer records must equal actual complete before/after
catalogue records. Only then does the original `qualifyLiveRestoration` mint its
private brand on the same complete objects consumed by original
`assertFreshRestoration`. A JSON status, copied proof or narrowed map cannot pass.
Original epoch-zero/Xmax/Xip bounds and all native claim/retry predicates remain
requirements. An unsupported native observation holds the result; it has no
waiver here.

Runtime source checks pin 45 root files, including the complete static local JS
import closure. Saved root files must equal reviewed `728a2c32` and current
committed objects. Immutable Git bindings may be cached for a specific HEAD and
pin set; every saved byte is hashed again on every phase. Disjoint descendant
commits are accepted only when every pinned input stays exactly equal. Executable
adapter files, pins and transfer metadata must also equal their own saved/index/
HEAD objects before any connection and on subsequent shared-turn phases. The
actual cwd, physical registered I2 project, Git worktree directory, common Git
directory and adapter source storage must resolve to the approved D: repository.
No machine configuration or shared Git metadata is repaired.

The future root protocol is finite:

1. Root reviews/publishes the exact source and invokes `hold-pure.mjs` with the
   physical I2 root, a fresh immediate child of its `.codex-tmp` named
   `daily-health-pure-native-20261017-<unique>`, and
   `--authorised-root-holder`. The original coordinator checks protected releases
   and takes the original non-waiting SEND_7 turn. BUSY/cooldown runs no trial.
2. A stays open. Fixed C-before closes. The process writes bounded `INPUT.json`,
   `INPUT_RECEIPT.json` and `TURN_IDENTITY.json`, then reports
   `READY_ROOT_KIER_MCP_B_REQUIRED`. Root dispatches that exact `INPUT.json`
   through the exact named Kier tool and saves its unchanged structured result
   as `NATIVE_RESULT.json`; send `PREPARE` on the process's stdin.
3. The process validates every successful statement, original final assertion,
   real B marker, genuine observations and small fresh MCP verification. Its
   separate fixed C-after reads full canonical snapshots and actual fixture
   proof. After original qualification succeeds it reports
   `QUALIFIED_PENDING_ROOT_RELEASE_AND_SHARED_TURN_CLOSE`; send `RELEASE`.
4. Only after the original coordinator confirms its own unlock and connection
   close may the bounded `SUMMARY.json` say PASS for this component. Full maps
   never enter files, console, control frames or the MCP envelope.

An unknown/early/duplicate command, ABORT, EOF, interrupt, turn loss, diagnostic,
transport cap or 120-second work deadline holds the run and closes only owned
local resources. The original small A connection is unchanged; C retains its
64-MiB stdout cap, 16-KiB diagnostic cap, 45-second statement bound and 70-second
child deadline. Work plus cleanup must finish within 180 seconds. An already
dispatched external MCP call cannot be cancelled by this local process: root
must reconcile its result before another trial. Never dispatch a stale READY
input after abort/timeout. No final PASS is emitted for unconfirmed cleanup.

Offline validation: 11 adapter tests and 44 unchanged original restoration/turn
tests pass. PG17 grammar parses the original programme, complete B, MCP
verification and both C source examples without substitutions; native body
compilation remains NOT_PROVED. `OFFLINE_INPUTS.json` contains **synthetic source
examples, never dispatch inputs or native evidence**. Tests cover real-marker
evidence requirements, assertion/statement envelopes, distinct backend IDs,
complete scope, original WeakMap copy refusal, parent/fixture/writer/ledger
refusals, caps, malformed UTF-8, finite controls and elapsed bounds.
